issue.title: Use each article’s cover in LinkedIn and social link previews
issue.body:
## Original request and outcome

Maintainer request (2026-11-09): “Зараз коли я вставляю будь яке посилання на мій сайт, скажемо на статтю, то в лінкедін превью картинка — мое фото. Я би хотів щоб превью картинки для статей принаймні — брались в таких випадках із титульної картинки самоі статті.”

When someone shares a native author-site article URL on LinkedIn, its preview should use that article's own title/hero image. Apply this through the existing publication/production metadata pipeline so current and future published articles behave consistently. This issue authorizes intake/planning only; implementation, PR and publication are separate steps under the existing workflow.

Example: https://vitaliioborskyi.ai/articles/the-sdlc-is-out-of-balance.html

## Verified source findings — 2026-11-09

Inspected main and production both point to `fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223` (tree `721eabb59e2814f03d328a4665a9b5cdcb067651`). The reported LinkedIn preview is the maintainer's observation; a new LinkedIn scrape/live HTML capture was not performed during this issue intake.

- [site/content/production-social.json](https://github.com/oborskyivitalii/oborskyivitalii/blob/fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223/site/content/production-social.json) declares the portrait `assets/vitalii-oborskyi.jpg`, JPEG960×887, alt “Portrait of Vitalii Oborskyi”.
- [tools/release/edition.cjs](https://github.com/oborskyivitalii/oborskyivitalii/blob/fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223/tools/release/edition.cjs#L17) pins that descriptor and inserts the same `og:image` / `twitter:image` metadata into production documents, including native articles.
- [tools/release/edition-archive.cjs](https://github.com/oborskyivitalii/oborskyivitalii/blob/fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223/tools/release/edition-archive.cjs#L104) explicitly requires article social tags to equal the principal-page tags. Its image-path validator currently admits only `assets/<filename>`; article media use their existing content-addressed closure.
- [tools/release/live.cjs](https://github.com/oborskyivitalii/oborskyivitalii/blob/fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223/tools/release/live.cjs#L11) verifies the single social descriptor returned by the edition verifier. Updating only a meta tag will leave production/archive/live assumptions inconsistent.
- Existing authored article owners: `site/publications/<id>/publication.json`, its validated article/assets/profile model, `tools/publishing/` and `tools/site/`. The SDLC source is [publication.json](https://github.com/oborskyivitalii/oborskyivitalii/blob/fe7baab277a8b90de330a1cec738b7085faf7223/site/publications/sdlc-out-of-balance/publication.json). Reuse the actual declared hero/cover selection; do not choose an arbitrary inline image or duplicate the manuscript/assets into a new SEO subsystem.

Only root AGENTS.md exists in the inspected tree. Repository map, README, AGENTS, dated MEMORY, CONTRIBUTING, site source contract and SEO/release owners were inspected. The dated MEMORY stable-only status is superseded by actual production refs and the delivery evidence in #177. No duplicate open issue was found in the current open inventory or exact og:image issue search.

## Scope and expected behavior

1. Give native published articles article-specific social metadata in their initial static HTML, available to crawlers without executing JavaScript. Reuse the same authored cover selection that presents the article's title image.
2. Reuse a suitable existing web rendition, or deterministically derive a social rendition from that cover using the existing media pipeline. Prefer 1200×630 (approximately1.91:1) JPEG, within LinkedIn's documented5MB limit and at least1200×627. Preserve the meaningful composition/title; use a deliberate crop or padding, not distortion. Keep provenance and applicable reuse/crop rights.
3. Set one authoritative `og:image`, type, actual dimensions and meaningful article-specific alt; keep existing Twitter-card image fields consistent. Use an absolute HTTPS URL on the canonical production origin, with complete frozen asset closure and correct MIME.
4. Every article uses its own cover, including future accepted articles. Canonical .html and supported extensionless entry forms must identify the same article/preview. Draft/unlisted/technical selection and snapshot isolation retain existing publication rules.
5. Proposed routine default: principal non-article pages keep the existing site image; a public article with no declared cover keeps a documented existing fallback. A declared but missing/invalid cover must be detected rather than silently selecting an unrelated image. Confirm this rule in requirements review before dependent implementation if current authoring contracts differ.
6. Update production, frozen-archive and live verifiers to check the correct image for each document, not global equality. Preserve exact old immutable releases/retained bytes and rollback compatibility using their own frozen evidence; no rewriting historical notices/images or blanket validator bypass.
7. Regenerate dependent output/identities and include any derived image in the existing artifact, media, rights and retention inventories. Edit authored owners; generated docs are output.

## Test impact and execution order

- Before implementation: follow current AGENTS/CONTRIBUTING, complete independent requirements review and a bounded test-impact map for the actual delta. Read applicable CODE-STYLE, ARTICLE-WORKFLOW, SITE-SEO, SITE-CHECK-PROFILES and production/rights contracts.
- Trace the cover from publication model through production metadata, article canonical/alias HTML, public asset inventory, archive validation and live HTTP verification.
- Inspect/update existing tests before advancing broad staging: `tests/site-articles.test.cjs`, `article-media.test.cjs`, `article-delivery.test.cjs`, `edition-retention.test.cjs`, `release-archive.test.cjs`, `release-controller.test.cjs`, `release-rights.test.cjs` and any actual production-social consumers found through source inventory. These are candidate impacted owners, not an instruction to rerun every suite without assessment.
- Add bounded behavior checks for distinct article covers, future publication selection, no-cover fallback, missing/invalid image, duplicate/stale metadata, source/hash/MIME/dimension mismatch and preserved historical restore. Prefer representative real producer output over assertions that simply repeat the implementation.
- Run targeted/source checks, regenerate and verify RI as applicable, obtain existing independent roles, then follow preview → maintainer review → stable staging → maintainer review → separately authorized production. Preserve current profile coverage and budgets; diagnose any failure before rerunning.
- After verified production: inspect raw served article HTML and image response, then refresh/check that exact article URL in LinkedIn Post Inspector. Record the actual preview or precise blocker. Do not create or publish a LinkedIn post as part of verification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC01 — Correct article selection.** Every eligible native article with a declared cover emits its own cover-derived `og:image` in initial static HTML; two distinct article inputs demonstrate distinct images. Current SDLC article uses its own hero. No JavaScript execution is needed.
- [ ] **AC02 — Usable preview image.** Image bytes, absolute URL, MIME, dimensions, size and alt match the declared frozen metadata and the LinkedIn sharing requirements. Composition is visually reviewed; no stretched image or accidental portrait substitution.
- [ ] **AC03 — Consistent routes and fallback.** Canonical/declared alias routes agree; principal pages and no-cover articles follow the documented fallback. Declared-invalid media, drafts and unrelated inline images cannot silently become a valid article preview.
- [ ] **AC04 — Delivery and history integrity.** Production, archive, live checks, rights/media inventory and retention support per-article images; historical immutable releases and rollback still verify without changing their original bytes or weakening guards.
- [ ] **AC05 — Reviewed and tested change.** Test impact is mapped before broad runs; affected source/profile checks and independent reviews pass on the exact candidate. Existing authorized release gates and budgets remain.
- [ ] **AC06 — Actual LinkedIn result.** After separately authorized production, exact served HTML/image are verified and LinkedIn Post Inspector shows the article cover after refresh; keep a screenshot/result and source/deployment/URL evidence. If blocked, record BLOCKED and keep this criterion open rather than treating generated metadata as platform proof.

## External behavior and references

LinkedIn uses Open Graph metadata; its official sharing guidance currently specifies a maximum5MB image, minimum1200×627 and recommended1.91:1:
https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a521928/make-your-website-shareable-on-linkedin

LinkedIn can cache previous URL previews. Post Inspector refreshes the URL for new shares; LinkedIn states previews in existing posts remain unchanged:
https://www.linkedin.com/help/linkedin/answer/a6233775
https://www.linkedin.com/post-inspector/

## Boundaries and related work

- No site redesign, new cover artwork, new analytics service, DNS changes, global replacement of the portrait, or LinkedIn/Medium post/account edits.
- This is article link-preview metadata, not the Medium canonical setting, and does not reopen #177's completed analytics delivery.
- Related owners/history: #159 (shared SEO infrastructure), #169 (native SDLC publication), #177 (analytics delivery and recorded remaining original SEO items), #8 (search/canonical observations). Keep this explicit new maintainer-requested issue as execution owner for the social-preview change.
